claims.text: Changing the relative concentrations of magnetic 3d elements in non-equiatomic HEAs can tune magnetic ordering.
Changing the relative concentrations of magnetic 3d elements in non-equiatomic HEAs can tune the magnetocaloric response.
The proposed material is a non-equiatomic HEA based on 3d transition metals.
The proposed initial alloy has a single-solid-solution or closely related structure.
The proposed initial alloy exhibits paramagnetic or soft-ferromagnetic behavior at room or low temperatures.
The ratios of magnetic components can be systematically varied during alloy synthesis.
Non-magnetic dopants may be introduced as an additional compositional-tuning method.
Compositional changes modify the local atomic environment and phase or site occupancy.
Changes in local environment and occupancy modify exchange interactions and local lattice distortion.
Altered elemental ratios modify exchange interactions.
Altered elemental ratios modify spin fluctuations, including longitudinal spin fluctuations.
Longitudinal spin fluctuations affect magnetic-moment formation in 3d-transition-metal HEAs.
Composition-induced changes in exchange interactions and spin fluctuations alter the magnetic entropy change at a phase transition.
Changing the magnetic entropy change tunes the magnetocaloric effect.
Non-equiatomic composition will produce systematic changes in magnetic transition temperature.
Non-equiatomic composition will produce systematic changes in adiabatic temperature change or isothermal entropy change.
Effective tuning requires retention of a single-phase or controlled multiphase structure.
Excessive compositional variation may cause phase separation or degraded magnetic order.
First-principles studies on 3d-based HEAs support the qualitative compositional-tuning effect.
Quantitative composition-dependent magnetic and magnetocaloric shifts, particularly in low-dimensional forms, remain to be experimentally calibrated.
